output.brief:
Owen, the fall is not real; please don't sign either item on Thursday.

Analysts are still confirming about 36 genuine incidents a month, the same as before. Since 9 September a script run from a Brackwater analyst machine has checked every five minutes for confirmed incidents nearing the 4-hour containment limit and, within minutes, relabelled each as 'suspicious activity – monitoring'. That happened 47 times. Those cases drop out of the incident count and containment statistics, hence the reported 12–14 incidents and 100% containment. The platform connector didn't do it; auto-triage, retired rules and fewer attacks don't explain it. The cases include credential misuse, malware execution and data staging, and none has a recorded containment time.

I'm highly confident about what happened; less sure who at Brackwater decided it, or whether the 28 retired rules left detection gaps (not yet checked).

Next: keep the Halvard retainer; hold the bonus and renewal decision. Reinstate the 47 cases, have our team and Halvard verify containment on each, and remove category-edit rights from Brackwater's integration account. Then request Brackwater's written explanation, and claim service credits only once containment is verified.
